questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Mia and Sam are talking at lunch. Mia is still speaking. What should Sam do?
choices: Talk louder so Mia hears him
Wait until Mia finishes, then speak
questions.explanation: Good conversations use turn-taking. Sam waits until Mia has finished before he speaks.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Jack is meeting the school principal for the first time. Which sentence is the most formal?
choices: Good morning, Mrs Nguyen. It is nice to meet you.
questions.explanation: Formal language is polite and uses full sentences and titles like Mrs. This is right for meeting a principal.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which sentence shows the strongest feeling about doing homework?
questions.explanation: The word must is the strongest. It means there is no choice. Might and could are weak.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Tom says, "It will rain today." He is not very sure. Which word makes his sentence weaker?
questions.explanation: Might shows that Tom is not sure. Words like must and definitely sound very sure.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: A science report says how to test which paper towel soaks up the most water. Which feature would you expect to find in it?
choices: A list of materials and the steps of the test
Rhyming words at the end of each line
A character who has a big problem
A speech bubble for each person
questions.explanation: Science texts often list materials and steps. Stories have characters and problems, and poems have rhymes.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: A text begins, "Once upon a time, a kangaroo lost her hat." What kind of text is it most likely to be?
questions.explanation: Starting with 'Once upon a time' and having a character with a problem tells us it is a story.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Ella writes about koalas. One paragraph tells what koalas eat. Which sentence belongs in that paragraph?
choices: Koalas sleep for up to 18 hours a day.
Koalas live in the eastern part of Australia.
questions.explanation: A paragraph keeps sentences about one idea together. Only the leaves sentence is about food.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: A new paragraph usually starts when the writer moves to a new idea.
questions.explanation: Each paragraph groups sentences about one idea. We start a new one for a new idea.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: On a website, Liam wants to go back to the first page. Which word would he look for?
questions.explanation: The Home button takes you to the first page of a website.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: A book has a list near the front. It shows each chapter name and its page number. What is this list called?
questions.explanation: The contents page lists chapters in order with page numbers. A glossary explains words and an index is at the back.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which sentence has a subject and a verb that match?
choices: The dogs runs in the park.
The dog run in the park.
The dogs run in the park.
The dog are running in the park.
questions.explanation: Dogs is more than one, so the verb is run. One dog would need runs.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which group of words is a full clause with a subject and a verb?
questions.explanation: Mum is the subject and bought is the verb. The other groups are missing one of these.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which word in this sentence is a thinking verb? "Zara wonders why the sky is blue."
questions.explanation: Wonders tells what Zara does in her mind, so it is a thinking verb.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses a saying verb?
choices: The cat jumped onto the fence.
questions.explanation: Whispered tells how Anna spoke, so it is a saying verb.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which sentence tells about something that has already happened?
choices: We will swim at the beach.
We are swimming at the beach.
questions.explanation: Swam is the past tense of swim. It shows the swimming is finished.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Write the past tense of the verb in this sentence. Today I run to school. Yesterday I ___ to school.
questions.explanation: Run is an irregular verb. Its past tense is ran, not runned.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which meaning of the word bat fits this sentence? "The cricketer swung the bat."
choices: A flying animal that sleeps upside down
A piece of wood used to hit a ball
questions.explanation: The sentence is about cricket, so bat means the piece of wood used to hit the ball.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: In maths, the word "table" can mean rows and columns of numbers. Which sentence uses table in this maths way?
choices: Dad set the table for dinner.
The table shows how many goals each player scored.
The table is made of wood.
Please put the plates on the table.
questions.explanation: A table that shows goals scored is rows and columns of information. The other tables are pieces of furniture.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Which word is the correct short form of "do not"?
questions.explanation: The apostrophe takes the place of the missing letter o. So do not becomes don't.

questions.subject: english
questions.prompt: Two girls share one cricket bat. Which sentence shows the bat belongs to both girls?
questions.explanation: For more than one owner ending in s, we put the apostrophe after the s: girls'.
